es: Usar verbos de estado y adjetivos en continuo para expresar conducta temporal o actitud (you're being silly, I'm loving it) y elegir entre simple y continuo según el matiz.

teaching.en: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because you are usually the most sensible person in the office.
teaching.es: Hoy estás haciendo el tonto, lo cual es impropio de ti, porque normalmente eres la persona más sensata de la oficina.
teaching.explanationEs: Be + being + adjetivo habla de la conducta de hoy; out of character señala que no es lo habitual en esa persona.
segments: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because
you are usually the most sensible person in the office.
teaching.audioText: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because you are usually the most sensible person in the office.

teaching.en: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.
teaching.es: Normalmente es educado, pero esta semana está siendo grosero con todos, y esperamos que sea solo algo temporal.
teaching.explanationEs: He's being rude es conducta de esta semana; He is rude sería su carácter.
segments: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude
to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.
teaching.audioText: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.

teaching.en: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.
teaching.es: Nuestra profesora es estricta por naturaleza, pero últimamente está siendo especialmente estricta con los deberes, y toda la clase lo ha notado.
teaching.explanationEs: El continuo destaca un cambio: lately refuerza que es algo reciente, distinto de lo normal.
segments: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being
unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.
teaching.audioText: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.

teaching.en: He's being stubborn about the plan, but for the time being nobody wants to argue with him.
teaching.es: Se está poniendo terco con el plan, pero de momento nadie quiere discutir con él.
teaching.explanationEs: For the time being indica algo provisional; combina bien con be being porque ambos hablan de lo temporal.
segments: He's being stubborn about the plan, but for the
time being nobody wants to argue with him.
teaching.audioText: He's being stubborn about the plan, but for the time being nobody wants to argue with him.

teaching.en: You're being annoying, so please stop; I'm not saying you are an annoying person, only that your behaviour is irritating right now.
teaching.es: Estás siendo pesado, así que para, por favor; no digo que seas una persona pesada, solo que tu comportamiento resulta irritante ahora mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: Being annoying critica una conducta del momento; is annoying describiría a la persona.
segments: You're being annoying, so please stop; I'm not saying you are
an annoying person, only that your behaviour is irritating right now.
teaching.audioText: You're being annoying, so please stop; I'm not saying you are an annoying person, only that your behaviour is irritating right now.

teaching.en: I'm loving my new job lately, although my sister says I've been a bit moody since the move.
teaching.es: Últimamente me está encantando mi nuevo trabajo, aunque mi hermana dice que estoy algo de mal humor desde la mudanza.
teaching.explanationEs: I'm loving es un uso coloquial y enfático de love; moody describe un humor cambiante, no un rasgo fijo.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige la frase que describe la conducta de Tom esta semana.

choices.text: He is rude, which is typical of him.
He is being rude, which is out of character for him.
He has been rude since he was a child.

feedback.es: Tom suele ser amable: is being rude describe una conducta de esta semana, distinta de su forma de ser, y out of character lo confirma.

hint.es: Busca la forma que marca una conducta temporal y no un rasgo de carácter.

origin.text: Tom is normally the friendliest person on the team, but this week he has hardly said hello, and yesterday he answered a simple question with one word.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sueles ser generoso, ¿por qué hoy estás siendo tan terco con el precio?»

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo de conducta (stubborn), el continuo de be lleva being: are you being stubborn, para un comportamiento de hoy.

hint.es: Es la forma -ing de be que marca conducta temporal.

origin.text: You're usually so generous, so why are you ___ so stubborn about the price today?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hoy está siendo muy generoso con su tiempo.»

answer.text: He is being very generous with his time today
accepted: He is being very generous with his time today
Today he is being very generous with his time

feedback.es: Be being + adjetivo da el matiz de conducta de hoy; very va delante del adjetivo y with his time dice en qué es generoso.

hint.es: Empieza por He is being y deja today para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la narradora sobre la conducta de su hermana.

choices.text: It shows that her real character has changed for good.
It was typical of her, because she is stubborn by nature.
It was unusual for her and probably linked to stress.

feedback.es: La narradora dice que fue out of character y temporal, y que su hermana está estresada: no es un cambio definitivo ni un rasgo fijo.

origin.audio: My sister has always been shy, so when she started talking loudly at dinner last night, we all looked at her. She was being very stubborn about where to go on holiday, and she even interrupted our father, which is completely out of character. Later she explained that she has been stressed lately and that her behaviour was only temporary. She promised that for the time being she would try to be more patient, and my father just laughed and said he was loving the new version of her.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el matiz que transmite.

pairs.es: Su conducta de hoy: suele no serlo
Reproche suave por una conducta concreta

feedback.es: Be + adjetivo describe el carácter; be being, la conducta del momento; I'm loving es un énfasis informal y You're being silly critica una acción concreta.

pairs.es: Su conducta de hoy: suele no serlo

prompt.es: Lee la nota. ¿Qué deduce la jefa sobre Carlos?

choices.text: That his attitude is temporary and probably has a cause.
That Carlos is a strict person who will never change.
That the new schedule was designed by Carlos himself.

feedback.es: He has never been like this before y something is worrying him sugieren que la severidad es temporal y tiene una causa, no un rasgo fijo.

origin.text: Note from the manager: 'Carlos is being very strict about the new schedule, and several people have mentioned it. He has never been like this before, so I suspect that something is worrying him.'

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige qué actitud muestra el narrador hacia Leo.

choices.text: Angry and ready to end the friendship for good.
Confused but understanding, since he sees it as a passing stage.
Pleased, because he finds Leo's behaviour rather funny.

feedback.es: El narrador no entiende a Leo, pero atribuye su conducta a los exámenes y la llama temporal: confusión con comprensión, no enfado ni burla.

origin.audio: I honestly don't know what has got into Leo lately. He is usually so generous, but this week he's being stubborn about everything. On Monday he refused to share the taxi, and yesterday he wouldn't lend Mia a pen. I suppose it is only temporary, because his exams are coming, but it is certainly out of character.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué dice el narrador sobre cómo es Leo normalmente.

choices.text: He is usually stubborn about small matters.
He has always refused to share with others.
He is usually generous with his things.

feedback.es: El narrador contrasta He is usually so generous con la conducta terca de esta semana: lo habitual en Leo es la generosidad.

origin.audio: I honestly don't know what has got into Leo lately. He is usually so generous, but this week he's being stubborn about everything. On Monday he refused to share the taxi, and yesterday he wouldn't lend Mia a pen. I suppose it is only temporary, because his exams are coming, but it is certainly out of character.

prompt.es: Completa: «Gritar al camarero fue impropio de él, que es muy educado.»

feedback.es: Out of character es la colocación para algo impropio de una persona; aquí contrasta con su fama de educado.

origin.text: Shouting at the waiter was completely ___ of character for him, because he is usually the politest man I know.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hoy está siendo inusualmente estricta con las nuevas normas.»

answer.text: She is being unusually strict about the new rules today
accepted: She is being unusually strict about the new rules today
Today she is being unusually strict about the new rules

feedback.es: She is being + unusually + adjetivo marca una conducta de hoy fuera de lo normal; about introduce aquello sobre lo que es estricta.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué sugiere la columnista sobre el enfado de su vecino?

choices.text: That the noise is a cover for another problem he has not mentioned.
That the noise really is impossible and must be reported.
That he has always complained about every single sound.

feedback.es: Normally a kind man y an excuse for something else sugieren que el ruido es un pretexto: la columnista sospecha de otro problema oculto.

origin.text: Columnist: 'My neighbour is being impossible this month. He is normally a kind man, yet now he complains about every noise. I'm trying to be patient, because I suspect that the noise is only an excuse for something else that is bothering him.'

prompt.es: Completa: «No recuerdo dónde vive, aunque lo conozco muy bien.»

feedback.es: Know es un verbo de estado y se queda en presente simple: I know him, nunca I am knowing him.

origin.text: I can't remember where he lives now, although I ___ him very well.

prompt.es: Escucha el reproche y elige qué distinción hace la hablante.

choices.text: She says his character is annoying every single day.
She criticises his behaviour today, not his character.
She regrets her own behaviour and says she is sorry.

feedback.es: La hablante separa la conducta de hoy (being annoying) del carácter (an annoying person): critica una acción, no a la persona.

origin.audio: You're being really annoying today, and I'm not saying you are an annoying person. I'm saying that your behaviour this afternoon is starting to bother me, so please stop.
